subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm designing a six-wheeled railgun carrier with deployable stabilizer legs and a long barrel on the turret, keeping it mostly static but adding a few joints for the turret and legs to allow movement.

I'm working out dimensions: a roughly 9-meter hull, wheel sizes and axle placement, cab position, turret and elevated barrel geometry pointing forward, and stabilizer leg placement, making sure overall proportions stay consistent and the barrel height clears the hull.

I'm sketching the box-based helper functions for building the hull and parts.

Now I'm planning camo paint patterns for the hull using patch and countershade techniques, importing the glow kit, then defining the joint hierarchy—hull root, turret, gun pivot, and wheel joints oriented along the x-axis for rolling motion—before moving on to designing the deployable stabilizer legs.

Each leg attaches at the hull sides and angles down to a foot pad, built from a rod connecting hull to pad plus a hydraulic piston assembly of nested cylinders, with a box beam housing where it meets the hull. I'm also thinking through decal textures—insignia emblems, warning chevrons, unit markings, and glowing details—to add to the hull surface.

I'm settling on around five textures: a hazard chevron pattern, an insignia, serial text, a cab windscreen, and a radar/vent screen, applied as textured planes with glow effects on the display surfaces. I'm defining the color palette (olive, dark olive, tan, steel, gunmetal, rubber black, orange, cyan glow) and starting to block out the hull as a main box shape with these dimensions in model space.

Writing layout code...

I'm computing the normal vector for the windscreen plane, lifting it slightly off the slope, then sizing and placing it. I also need the nose front face geometry, a front bumper box with hazard stripes, and the rear deck panel starting from the hull top.

Now I'm turning to the turret: a ring cylinder joint at the hull, then building the turret body as an extruded side profile with sloped front and side cheeks, and placing the gun breech pivot relative to the turret front.

Working out the gun barrel geometry relative to the tilted pivot axis, with helper functions to translate local offsets into world positions and build rail rods along the barrel direction...

Adding the glow strips, muzzle brake, breech block, and cradle plates between rails, plus the elevation hydraulic rod. Positioning the barrel elevated 20° in firing mode, computing tip coordinates relative to the pivot so overhang clears the cab, and setting the wheel axle positions along the hull.

I'm adding rib discs to the tires for tread detail and fender boxes above the wheel arches, then adjusting the hull width to narrow the lower section so the wheels don't clip into the hull sides.

Now I'm placing mudguards over the tires and working out the stabilizer leg positions along the hull, checking the z-coordinates to ensure the legs sit in the gaps between wheel axles without overlapping the wheel radius spans.

I'm settling on four legs at z=1.5 and -1.3 on each side, plus a rear spade stabilizer, and designing each leg as a horizontal arm extending from the hull into a vertical piston mechanism with an outer cylinder, inner piston, and a round pad at the bottom.

Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy for each stabilizer, naming them systematically (stab1, stab2, etc.) and attaching them to the hull at the appropriate positions, deciding to skip adding a specific role tag for now and move on to specifying wheel joints next.

I'm planning out the wheel joints parented to the hull, and sketching the full set of greeble details I want to add: roof rails, antenna, radar dish, headlights and tail lights with glow effects, exhaust stacks, fuel tanks, camouflage netting, a rear capacitor bank with glowing vents, cable sweeps connecting it to the turret, plus ladders, handrails, tow hooks, hazard stripes, insignia, and vehicle numbering to give the model a lived-in, functional look.

Now I'm designing a procedural camouflage paint function that blends olive, dark, and tan tones using noise-based blobs, with darker shading toward the underside for realism. I'm also planning out the SVG textures I'll need: hazard chevron stripes, a star insignia, a serial number decal, and a windscreen texture with glass highlights.

I'm sketching more textures too -- a radar HUD screen, grille vents, hub bolts, and a warning triangle sign. Then I'm setting up a decal helper to place textured planes onto bones at specific positions and directions, and figuring out where to position hull and cab side panels so the insignia and other decals land correctly on the body.

Now I'm working out the hull's overall proportions -- raising its height, defining the chassis box dimensions, and positioning the front and rear axles. I'm also laying out the rear deck, placing the turret ring, capacitor bank, and hull-side tool boxes, then starting on the turret's joint position.

Working out turret geometry...

Raising the pivot to rel 1.25 so the breech sits above the roof rather than embedded, with the bottom at 2.65 inside. I'm adding trunnion side blocks flanking the pivot to anchor the gun mount visually.

Now I'm setting up the actual gun joint, defining its position relative to the turret and tilting its direction about 18 degrees upward. I need to work out the local axis orientation carefully since the model's right is flipped relative to world coordinates, but since the geometry is symmetric left-right, this ends up not mattering for the visual result.

Defining the barrel geometry...

Adding glow details to the rings, muzzle, and bore ends, then working out the elevation cylinder rod geometry connecting the turret to the barrel pivot point.

Now I'm sketching turret add-ons like hatch cylinders, sensor mast, smoke dischargers, camo side panels, antenna whips, cab window textures, door handles, and mirror arms, along with a front bumper box positioned near the cab.

I'm placing the hazard chevron plane on the bumper face, adding headlight glow boxes near the cab front corners, and shaping the grille plane to follow the front slope.

I realize there's a gap between chassis top at 1.2 and cab bottom at 1.95, so I need to extend the cab profile down to 1.15 to close that area. Adjusting the polygon points to run from (2.0,1.15) up through the roofline and back down to (4.3,1.15) keeps it a simple closed shape, and wheels at z2.9 sit outside the cab width.

For extrusion I'm setting the direction along +Z with thickness 2.6 centered on x, then applying camo paint across the whole hull. For the radar dish on the cab roof, I'm considering a lathe profile for a cone-ish shape, or possibly a squashed cylinder, to keep the dish simple.

I'm placing the dish at roughly (0.7, 3.15, 2.3) near the cab roof and adding a mast and small orange glowing light bar nearby. I'm also planning a rear ladder with rungs on the hull, a tail-light-equipped rear plate near z -4.0 with red glow lights, and an angled rear spade made from an extruded triangular profile.

Actually, with legs at that position I'll move the toolbox onto the deck instead, placing boxes near the front. I'm also adding a capacitor bank at the rear with glowing cylindrical caps on top, plus a cable sweep connecting the caps to the turret rear using a curved path.

Adding glow rings and cyan side indicator strips, and setting up a mirrored loop so decals and panels on both sides face outward correctly without text appearing reversed.

Windows stay unlit while screens get the emissive glow treatment. I'm adding exhaust stacks behind the cab as vertical cylinders with caps and vent tops, then planning the wheel loop generation to keep the total part count and code length manageable.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Now I'm setting up the stabilizer legs with joints at the hull, placing the arm boxes, pistons, and pads, then adding a hazard chevron plane facing upward on the arm.

Now I'm settling on the color palette for the camo variants and dark metal parts, and planning out the extrude helper's options like bevel for the turret cheeks before writing the full build code.

Checking the turret geometry math: joint position, roof height, gun pivot location, breech overlap with the roof, and barrel elevation angle to confirm the tip height works out reasonably for a railgun-style vehicle.

Now I'm working out the rod and rail attachment points, noting that local "right" maps to negative world X, so I need to flip the sign when placing symmetric left/right points consistently. I'll loop over the mirrored x-offsets for both the rods and the side rails, then finalize and write the export.
